source.title: When is early stopping beneficial under label noise? A phase diagram for kernel gradient flow

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures test error over training time and reports conditions with late deterioration as well as conditions where it is absent, refining the claim about epoch-wise behavior. It does not test the specified model-size, sample-size, or general capacity curves.
record.gate_note: Rows record the study's own test-error trajectories and its stated outcomes. Cited results from other work are excluded. The paper varies model capacity, data size, and noise fraction in some experiments, but those results do not establish the model-wise double-descent curve or that more data raises error near an interpolation threshold.
record.test_reason: The CIFAR10 networks are trained with 20% random labels and test error is tracked over up to 1500–2000 epochs, close to the epoch-wise double-descent setting. Larger, deeper networks show no late rise, and smaller or fixed-feature models rise with no second descent within the horizon. This bears on V2. The kernel analysis is a different system (fixed kernel gradient flow) and is recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Essentially correct. The authors add that the boundary γc(ε) depends only on the random-label fraction. At the critical kernel, the interpolating endpoint beats every early-stopped iterate across all kernels considered, a result stronger than benign overfitting. Optimally tuned ridge matches that error without interpolating.
record.recipe_differences: The study examines noisy-label test-error trajectories using CIFAR10 neural-network training and a synthetic RAF fixed-kernel gradient-flow analysis; it does not reproduce the original double-descent size sweep.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcome depends on kernel geometry relative to γc(ε), architecture and capacity, and training recipe. The paper also varies initialization, optimizer, batch size, sample size, and random-label fraction.

fits_no_version.finding: In fixed-kernel gradient flow on the RAF model with label noise and zero ridge, test error either decreases monotonically to interpolation (γ≤γc(ε)) or eventually increases toward t=∞ (γ>γc(ε)). In neither case is there a final second descent. The boundary is independent of α and the initialization. RBF simulations on synthetic data and on CIFAR10 show the same contrast.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For fixed kernels trained by gradient flow under label noise, whether late training hurts is set by kernel geometry (the linear versus higher-order component ratio), and the trajectory has no epoch-wise second descent.

record.problems: The neural-network evidence uses finite training horizons and noisy-label CIFAR10 settings; the reported best test performance is the best observed within those horizons. Several qualitative outcomes are reported for groups of architectures rather than separately for each model. The theoretical analysis assumes fixed smooth dot-product kernels and a high-dimensional RAF data model, and does not explain how feature-learning networks acquire the relevant geometry.

untested.parts: κ≈1,10,100 capacities are compared only for late-time deterioration. Final test error is not reported as a function of size around the interpolation threshold.
n is varied from 1536 to 9216, but the direction of test error with n near the threshold is not reported.
No capacity sweep across model classes past interpolation.
No effective-complexity measure predicting peak locations.
The label-noise fraction is varied (ε=0–0.8), but no peak is measured. Ridge is compared with gradient flow only in the kernel theory, not as a means of removing a peak.
Whether a second descent appears beyond 1500–2000 epochs for the smaller models that show a rise.

missing.what: Final-minus-minimum test-error gap (percentage points, 95% CI) for two-layer CNN, four-layer CNN and ResNet-16 at κ≈1.16 and κ≈447 across six optimizer protocols. Larger deep models show smaller gaps.

Random labels on cats and dogs instead of automobiles. Under square loss, deeper nets reach their minimum after zero memorization, but some retain a visible gap. Under cross-entropy, all five stay near their best.

record.verdict_notes: The study is framed around early stopping, not double descent. It cites Nakkiran et al. only as related work. The neural-network outcomes are qualitative, group-level statements over finite horizons. A late second descent for the smaller models cannot be excluded, and the absence of a rise in large models rests on visual descriptions. The kernel rows were relinked to none because V2 concerns deep networks.

versions.untested_parts: The study varies architecture and capacity but does not measure test error as a function of model size to test a fall-peak-fall curve near the size that just fits the training set.
The reported trajectories examine early stopping and late-time deterioration, not a complete fall-rise-fall double-descent curve with a subsequent second decline.
Training-set size is varied in controls, but the paper does not report that increasing sample size raises test error near an interpolation threshold.
The kernel analysis varies kernel geometry and training time, not model-class capacity across the interpolation point.
The study identifies a kernel-geometry threshold for its stopping behavior but does not test a single effective-complexity measure predicting peak locations across size, epochs, and samples.

The study varies label-noise fraction and discusses ridge regularization, but does not test whether a double-descent peak is driven by noise, splits into multiple peaks, or disappears under optimally tuned regularization.
The study does not recount complexity using an effective number of parameters or test whether this turns a second descent into an ordinary U-shaped curve.

rows.subject: kernel gradient flow on the RAF model

rows.measure: Rule generalization classification error Egen(τ) over training time
rows.value: Test error initially decreases, eventually increases, and has a minimum at finite positive time.
rows.note: This reports a decrease followed by deterioration, but not the subsequent second decrease in the claimed fall-rise-fall shape.

rows.operation_detail: Track clean test error and random-label memorization error during training.

conditions.value: CIFAR10 cats and dogs with randomly labelled automobiles
Square loss; no augmentation or weight decay

rows.measure: Clean test classification error over training time, alongside memorization error
rows.value: Fixed-feature and smaller or shallower models exhibit late-time test-error deterioration as memorization error decreases.
rows.uncertainty: Figure 1 averages about 30 completed seeds; Figure 8 reports pointwise 95% confidence intervals for means.
rows.note: The reported behavior includes late deterioration but does not establish a subsequent second descent. The text gives this outcome for the group, not separately for every model and capacity.
rows.check: The subject groups RF-CNN (fixed features, readout-only GD) with trainable two-layer CNNs. Only the trainable small CNNs are the deep-network system V2 names. There is a fall then rise and no observed second descent within 1500 epochs, which is a finite horizon.

rows.subject: larger, deeper convolutional and residual networks, reported collectively

rows.operation_detail: Track clean test error and random-label memorization error during training.

conditions.value: CIFAR10 cats and dogs with randomly labelled automobiles
Constant-rate Nesterov SGD through 1500 epochs; no augmentation or weight decay

rows.measure: Clean test classification error over training time, alongside memorization error
rows.value: Late-time test-error deterioration is essentially absent; best observed test performance is attained with zero memorization error.
rows.uncertainty: Figure 1 averages about 30 completed seeds; Figure 8 reports pointwise 95% confidence intervals for means.
rows.note: The authors describe a group-level result for larger and deeper networks, not separate numerical outcomes for each architecture.
rows.check: No late rise for larger/deeper CNNs and ResNets at 20% label noise. This is the setting where V2 predicts a fall-rise-fall curve. It is a group-level, qualitative statement.

rows.subject: four-layer CNN, six-layer CNN, ResNet-16, WRN-28, and MobileNetV2, reported collectively
rows.size_stated: Approximately 2.7 million optimized parameters per network
rows.operation_detail: Track clean test error and random-label memorization error during augmented cross-entropy training.

conditions.value: CIFAR10; 6144 training images, including randomly labelled automobiles
Augmentation, scheduled learning rate, cross-entropy; 2000 epochs except WRN-28 at 1000 epochs

rows.measure: Clean test classification error over training time, alongside memorization error
rows.value: Test error settles to an approximately constant plateau with zero memorization error; continued training preserves performance close to the best observed level, with little visible advantage from early stopping.
rows.uncertainty: Five training seeds; Figure 10 reports pointwise 95% confidence intervals for means.
rows.note: The paper reports the outcome collectively for the five architectures.
rows.check: Group-level result for five architectures; no rise after memorization under augmented cross-entropy.

rows.subject: full RBF-kernel gradient flow on CIFAR10
rows.operation_detail: Track test and memorization errors over time for several RBF bandwidths.

conditions.value: 3072 CIFAR10 training images; cats and dogs plus randomly labelled automobiles

rows.measure: Clean test classification error over training time, alongside memorization error
rows.value: For some kernels test error initially decreases and then rises as memorization is completed; for others the trajectory reaches interpolation with little or no observed loss of generalization.
rows.uncertainty: Five repetitions; curves show mean errors.
rows.note: The text does not map these qualitative outcomes to individual bandwidths. Neither outcome establishes a complete fall-rise-fall curve.
rows.check: Full RBF-kernel gradient flow on CIFAR10, a fixed kernel rather than a deep network. Bandwidths were chosen for illustration.

rows.subject: RBF kernel gradient flow on synthetic RAF data
rows.operation_detail: Compare analytical learning curves with finite-sample RBF simulations.

conditions.value: 12 independent realizations; 10000 fresh test inputs per realization

rows.measure: Generalization classification error over reduced training time
rows.value: Factual labels are memorized before generalization finishes improving; the test optimum is finite, with late deterioration described as weak.
rows.uncertainty: Figure 6 shows one standard error bars for simulation means.
rows.note: This is a decrease followed by some late deterioration, not a reported second descent.
rows.check: Kernel simulation validating the theory; not the V2 system.

rows.subject: ResNet-16 (WRN-16-4), reported across extended controls
rows.operation_detail: Measure test-error trajectories while varying sample size, batch size, random-label fraction, and training recipe.

conditions.value: Augmented cross-entropy and constant-rate square loss

rows.measure: Test classification error over training time
rows.value: Across displayed conditions with random labels, test performance approaches a plateau close to its lowest recorded value and remains stable through the end of training.
rows.uncertainty: Five seeds, with ten seeds at ε = 0.1 and 0.2 for Figure 12; Figure 12 gives one sample standard deviation.
